ruling.recommended_action: Refund $1.04 (waiting charge) to the rider as a Ryde voucher; no distance refund is due for the Clementi Mall stop; flag the driver account for repeat route disputes.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip was RydeTAXI and metered, so the fare tracks distance and waiting units [F8]; only RydeTAXI's metered structure makes extra kilometres chargeable at all [RD-2].

The single off-route segment (F4, 14:21–14:30, 3.80 km vs 2.10 km optimal, +1.70 km) was driven to reach a stop the rider named herself: the rider wrote "Can you stop at Clementi Mall?" at 14:17 and the driver agreed [F9][F10], and the car did stop there for 4 minutes [F2][F11]. Under RD-3(a) a rider-named stop is not a detour, so the whole segment driven to reach Clementi Mall is exempt and its extra kilometres are not refundable [RD-3][RD-1].

No other exemption or liability basis is triggered. There is no qualifying traffic incident on the replaced stretch [F14], and speed bands 4 and 5 on Ayer Rajah Expressway and Jurong Town Hall Road (30–49 km/h) are not band 1/2 and in any case merely corroborative [F12][F13][RD-4]; light rain alone is not a "reasonable cause" showing [F15]. No driver-proposed route with prior rider agreement appears, so RD-5 does not exempt anything on consent grounds [RD-5].

The waiting charge is a different matter. RD-3(c) requires a published basis before a mid-trip stop can be billed; Ryde publishes only a $5 pick-up waiting fee, so the $1.04 charged for 4 minutes of mid-trip stopping [F6] is not a published item and must be waived [RD-3]. The remaining $24.48 of the $25.52 fare stands: base $3.90, distance $14.88, time $4.23 and platform $1.47 [F8] are ordinary metered and published components, and the billed excess-distance figure of $2.79 (2.0 km × $1.41/km) [F5] is explained by the exempt segment.

Because the case establishes a route-deviation finding against the driver (recorded RD-1 breach) and the driver profile shows already-upheld route disputes (route_disputes_upheld_90d = 2) [F17], a repeat-breach account flag attaches [RD-6]. Profile facts are used only for that additional action, not to decide the deviation itself.

rejected_claims.reason: The rider cannot recover the excess distance: the only off-route segment was the drive to the Clementi Mall stop the rider herself named and the car stopped at, which RD-3(a) exempts in full [F9][F2][RD-3]; the billed excess of $2.79 (2.0 km × $1.41/km) is therefore not refundable [F5][RD-2].

The driver cannot keep the mid-trip waiting charge: no policy clause authorises billing 4 minutes of stopping at an intermediate point, since the only published waiting fee is the $5 pick-up fee [F6][RD-3], so $1.04 is waived under RD-3(c).

events.body:
This is a RydeTAXI metered trip, so the fare follows distance and waiting units [F8]; meter distance is the only reason extra kilometres could be chargeable, and the refund formula for an unexempt segment is extra_km × (distance_fare ÷ distance_km) [RD-2].

The single off-route segment (F4, 14:21–14:30, 3.80 km driven vs 2.10 km optimal, +1.70 km) exists and is code-settled [RD-1]. It was driven to reach a stop the rider named herself: at 14:17 she wrote "Can you stop at Clementi Mall?" and the driver agreed [F9][F10], and the car stopped there for 4 minutes [F2][F11]. Under RD-3(a) a rider-named stop is not a detour, so the whole segment driven to reach it is exempt and its extra kilometres are not refundable [RD-3]. No other basis applies: there is no qualifying incident on the replaced stretch [F14], and the Ayer Rajah Expressway (band 4, 30–39 km/h) and Jurong Town Hall Road (band 5, 40–49 km/h) records are neither band 1/2 nor exempting on their own [F12][F13][RD-4]; light rain is not a "reasonable cause" showing [F15]; and no driver-proposed route was agreed before leaving the optimal route [RD-5].

The disputed extra distance follows the exempt segment: the billed excess of $2.79 is 2.0 km × $1.41/km [F5], inside the exempted stretch [F4].

What remains outside RD-3(a) is the waiting charge, which RD-3(a)'s carve-out ("only the waiting fee rules apply") sends to RD-3(c): a mid-trip stop may only be billed on a published basis, and Ryde publishes a waiting fee solely for the pick-up point, not for intermediate stops [RD-3]. The $1.04 billed for 4.0 min of mid-trip stopping (4.0 min × $0.26/min) [F6] is therefore a fee without a published, satisfied condition and is waived, computed as 4.0 min × $0.26/min = $1.04 [F6][RD-3(c)]. The rest of the $25.52 stands: base $3.90, distance $14.88, time $4.23 and platform $1.47 [F8], as the record shows surge 1.0× and no discount [F7].

No account flag is applied. The excess-distance element of the dispute is not upheld because RD-3(a) exempts the segment [F4][RD-3], so RD-2 yields no non-exempt segment; the only refundable item is a waiting-fee waiver, which falls under RD-3 and not under the route-deviation repeat-breach trigger. The code trace likewise reports no qualifying non-exempt segment on which to base a flag [F17][RD-6].
